data.title: Oracle Expected Spending on Job Cuts Rises to $2.8 Billion
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan 




  Oracle plans to spend an additional $700 million on job cuts as part of a restructuring plan aimed at adopting artificial intelligence across its business. 



  The increase, which brings the total costs associated with its 2026 restructuring plan to $2.8 billion, reflects "additional actions that we expect to take," the software and cloud-computing company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. 



  As of Aug. 31, the company projected $2.1 billion in costs associated with the plan, according to the filing. 



  The majority of the costs accrued to date are tied to employee severance payments, and concentrated most heavily in Oracle's "other" and cloud and software segments. 



  Oracle's head count shrunk by roughly 13% in its latest fiscal year, which ended in May, according to its latest annual report. The company began the process of reducing its workforce in March, The Wall Street Journal reported. 



  Other tech firms have similarly shed workers as they spend heavily on building out AI infrastructure and look to boost efficiency with the help of AI technology.

data.title: KBRA Assigns an A Rating and Stable Outlook to St. Louis Lambert International Airport Revenue Bonds
data.description:
KBRA Assigns an A Rating and Stable Outlook to St. Louis Lambert International Airport Revenue Bonds

KBRA assigns a long-term rating of A with a Stable Outlook to the City of St. Louis, Missouri (the City) Airport Revenue Bonds Series 2026A (Federally Taxable), Series 2026B (AMT), and Series 2026C (Non-AMT) issued for St. Louis Lambert International Airport (the Airport). Concurrently, KBRA assigns an A rating to the City's outstanding Airport Revenue Bonds.

Proceeds of the Series 2026 Bonds to 1) finance elements of the Airport’s fiscal year (FY) 2027 – 2032 capital improvement plan (CIP) including a runway resurfacing project and planning for the future modernization of the Airport referred to as the Consolidated Terminal Program (CTP); 2) refund all or a portion of the Airport’s outstanding Junior Lien Bank Notes; 3) fund the required deposit to the debt service reserve fund; 4) pay capitalized interest; and 5) costs of issuance.

Airport Revenue Bonds (GARBs) are payable from the Net Revenues generated by the operation of the Airport.

Key Credit Considerations

Credit Positives

  • The service area’s broad and diverse economic base that generates consistent demand for air service bolstered by recent economic development activity including a Boeing defense aircraft assembly facility.
  • An essentially residual-based operating agreement that provides a base for sound financial operations and coverage of annual debt service.
  • Current moderate debt and cost structure which provides some capacity for the CTP, although details on its ultimate scope and financing strategy are unknown.

Credit Challenges

  • Local economic growth lags national trends limiting expectations for future gains in passenger volume.
  • Senior management transition at a time when the Airport is planning a significant capital program.
  • Moderately high pro-forma levels associated with the current CIP that are likely to trend higher with the planned terminal redevelopment.

Rating Sensitivities

For Upgrade

  • Sustained growth in enplanement growth leading to increased revenue capacity and moderating leverage.
  • Successful negotiation of a new use and lease agreement that materially strengthens the Airport’s financial and capital-planning framework.
  • Confirmation that the chosen CTP implementation and financing strategy results in a pro-forma cost and leverage profile which places the Airport at the lower end of peer medium hub airports undertaking capital programs of similar scope and complexity.

For Downgrade

  • A material reduction in service by Southwest Airlines or a prolonged economic contraction, resulting in a sustained decline in passenger activity and related revenues.
  • Confirmation that the chosen CTP implementation and financing strategy results in a pro-forma cost and leverage profile which places the Airport meaningfully above peer medium hub airports undertaking capital programs of similar scope and complexity.

To access ratings and relevant documents, click here.

Methodology

  • Public Finance: U.S. General Airport Revenue Bond Rating Methodology

Disclosures

A description of all substantially material sources that were used to prepare the credit rating and information on the methodology(ies) (inclusive of any material models and sensitivity analyses of the relevant key rating assumptions, as applicable) used in determining the credit rating is available in the Information Disclosure Form(s) located here.

Information on the meaning of each rating category can be located here.

Further disclosures relating to this rating action are available in the Information Disclosure Form(s) referenced above. Additional information regarding KBRA policies, methodologies, rating scales and disclosures are available at www.kbra.com.

About KBRA

Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC (KBRA), one of the major credit rating agencies (CRA), is a full-service CRA registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as an NRSRO. Kroll Bond Rating Agency Europe Limited is registered as a CRA with the European Securities and Markets Authority. Kroll Bond Rating Agency UK Limited is registered as a CRA with the UK Financial Conduct Authority. In addition, KBRA is designated as a Designated Rating Organization (DRO) by the Ontario Securities Commission for issuers of asset-backed securities to file a short form prospectus or shelf prospectus. KBRA is also recognized as a Qualified Rating Agency by Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission and is recognized by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners as a Credit Rating Provider (CRP) in the U.S.

data.title: Scholar Rock Gets FDA Approval of Isembyld for Spinal Muscular Atrophy
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman 




  Scholar Rock said the Food and Drug Administration approved Isembyld, or apitegromab, for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy. 



  The drug was approved for adults and for children two years of age and older who are currently receiving a survival motor neuron 2-targeted treatment. 



  Scholar Rock said Friday that Isembyld will be available to ship in the coming days. 



  The company said it was awarded a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher, which may be used to obtain priority review for a future marketing application. 



  In August, Scholar Rock said that under FDA guidance, it successfully removed Catalent Indiana as a commercial fill-finish facility and that the FDA review was progressing well with an alternate fill-finish facility. At the time, Scholar Rock said it was prepared for a launch immediately upon FDA approval. 



  Scholar Rock shares were halted after hours for pending news.

data.title: Stellantis Talks With Canadian Workers Hit Impasse on Plan to Sell Ontario Factory, Union Says — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira 




  OTTAWA--Stellantis is in talks to sell its idled Toronto-area factory to a local defense firm, prompting the union representing more than 9,000 of the automaker's Canadian employees to declare an impasse on talks toward a new labor deal. 



  The potential sale is the latest development involving the Stellantis factory in Brampton, Ontario, which hasn't operated since 2024 to undergo retooling yet has emerged as a flashpoint in the tariff conflict between Ottawa and Washington. 



  Stellantis last year unveiled plans to shift the production of its next-generation Jeep Compass to Illinois from Brampton amid hefty Trump administration tariffs on foreign-made cars. The decision sparked the threat of a lawsuit from the Canadian government, which had provided Stellantis with hundreds of millions for work at the plants in Brampton and Windsor, Ontario. 



  Unifor, which represents auto-assembly workers, said Stellantis disclosed during talks on a new collective-bargaining agreement that the company had an interested buyer of the Brampton plant in a Canadian producer of smart-armored vehicles. 



  A Stellantis spokeswoman confirmed the interest from Canadian defense manufacturer Roshel, a maker of armored vehicles. Stellantis added that the two sides have signed a memorandum of understanding, which signals both companies' interest in pursuing a transaction. 



   "The persistence of the company's proposal to close and sell the Brampton plant has hindered the bargaining process," Unifor said, adding that talks have reached an impasse and are now paused. Unifor said the current labor deal expires on Aug. 20. 



  The Stellantis spokeswoman said Roshel represents the best option to restoring operations at its Brampton assembly plant, "preserving the site's strategic role in Canada's advanced manufacturing sector and helping to avoid a prolonged period of inactivity." She had no further comment, citing collective-bargaining talks with Unifor. 



  In a statement, Roshel chief executive Roman Shimonov said the company is willing to make commitments to affected Stellantis workers about employment. "We look forward to successfully concluding our discussions with Stellantis and implementing our plans to bring over 2,000 jobs," Shimonov said. 



  The Mayor of Brampton, Patrick Brown, said he was disappointed. "With this news, the promise of future work from Stellantis appears to be yet another broken commitment," Brown said. "Stellantis should not be allowed to take federal money and abandon Brampton and Canada." 



  Government officials have been in talks about the future of the Brampton plant. A spokesman for Canada's Department of Industry said any sale of the plant would need to comply with commitments Stellantis made regarding employment when the company accepted government financing. Industry Minister Melanie Joly has threatened a lawsuit against Stellantis, for failing to follow through with the Jeep Compass production, and vowed to recover the millions of dollars that governments provided to the car maker. 



  Trade relations between the U.S. and Canada have deteriorated in the past three weeks after talks unexpectedly collapsed toward a new trade pact, with both sides blaming the other for raising last-minute demands. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the negotiations with the U.S. revealed that the Trump administration wanted "to destroy our major industries, including our auto industry."

data.title: FCEL CLASS ACTION NOTICE: Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Files Securities Fraud Lawsuit On Behalf Of FuelCell Energy, Inc. Investors
data.description:
FCEL CLASS ACTION NOTICE: Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Files Securities Fraud Lawsuit On Behalf Of FuelCell Energy, Inc. Investors

Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP (“GPWR”), announces that it has filed a class action lawsuit in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, captioned Nguyen v. FuelCell Energy, Inc., et al., Case No. 1:26-cv-07953, on behalf of persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired FuelCell Energy, Inc. (“FuelCell” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: FCEL) securities between June 24, 2026 and September 1, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). Plaintiff pursues claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Exchange Act”).

Investors are hereby notified that they have 60 days from the date of this notice to move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff in this action.

IF YOU SUFFERED A LOSS ON YOUR FUELCELL ENERGY, INC. INVESTMENTS, CLICK HERE TO INQUIRE ABOUT POTENTIALLY PURSUING CLAIMS TO RECOVER YOUR LOSS UNDER THE FEDERAL SECURITIES LAWS.

What Happened?

On September 2, 2026, before the market opened, FuelCell reported its fiscal third quarter 2026 financial results, reporting a net loss of $45.3 million. According to the Company’s press release, this reflected “a higher gross loss than the prior year period,” which was caused by “product costs and manufacturing overhead that currently exceed the contractual pricing established under the CEPA with Fit Energy.” Further, FuelCell reported that the annualized production rate was “below the production volume at which we expect our cost structure to align with market-based pricing for orders of this scale,” and as a result, the Company recorded a $17 million charge to “reflect the impact of contractual pricing provisions associated with specific inventory and firm purchase commitments” arising from Phase 0 of the CEPA.

On this news, FuelCell shares fell $2.68, or 15.69%, to close at $14.40 per share on September 2, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What Is The Lawsuit About?

The complaint filed in this class action alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that the Company’s manufacturing capacity was inadequate to generate the production rate required under the CEPA; (2) that, as a result, the Company’s annualized production rate for deliveries under the CEPA with Fit Energy was slower than expected; (3) that, as a result, the Company was incurring higher product costs and manufacturing overhead expenses; (4) that, as a result of the slower production rate, the Company was reasonably likely to incur charges in connection with the CEPA; (5) that the foregoing was a known trend affecting the Company’s profitability; and (6) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants’ positive statements about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

If you purchased or otherwise acquired FuelCell Energy, Inc. securities during the Class Period, you may move the Court no later than 60 days from the date of this notice to ask the Court to appoint you as lead plaintiff.

data.title: Boo Bash Fall Festival to Make California Debut September 18, Bringing 100,000+ Square-Foot Immersive Pumpkin Patch to Escondido
data.description:
Boo Bash Fall Festival to Make California Debut September 18, Bringing 100,000+ Square-Foot Immersive Pumpkin Patch to Escondido

Boo Bash Fall Festival to Make California Debut September 18, Bringing 100,000+ Square-Foot Immersive Pumpkin Patch to Escondido

PR Newswire

ESCONDIDO, Calif., Sept. 11, 2026

New seasonal experience will transform Mershops North County Mall into a six-week fall destination with five distinct zones and programming for all ages

ESCONDIDO, Calif., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boo Bash, a seasonal pumpkin patch and family fall festival, will make its California debut on Friday, September 18 at Mershops North County Mall in Escondido, transforming the mall parking lot into a six-week fall destination with seasonal attractions, activities and entertainment through November 1.

Spanning five distinct zones, Boo Bash will offer a mix of classic fall traditions, interactive attractions and seasonal entertainment for guests of all ages. The six-week experience will feature pumpkins available for purchase, local food and retail vendors, seasonal displays, photo opportunities, panning for gems, a 60-foot pumpkin bounce pad, a petting zoo, a children's racetrack, inflatable attractions, zorb balls, face painting, carnival games and more.

Boo Bash will also host live music every Friday and Saturday night, along with select movie nights and rotating family entertainment throughout the season.

"We're thrilled to bring Boo Bash to California for the first time. We chose Escondido because North County is a growing, vibrant community that deserves a large-scale fall destination of its own. Our goal is to create an affordable experience where people of all ages can come together and enjoy the best of fall and Halloween." said Jack Bruce, Executive Producer and owner at 365 Entertainment Group.

Boo Bash will run from September 18 through November 1 at Mershops North County Mall in Escondido. The festival will be open Monday through Thursday from 3:00 to 9:00 p.m., Friday from 3:00 to 10:00 p.m., Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and Sunday from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.

Tickets for entry start at $5 and can be purchased at www.boobashescondido.com/tickets. General admission includes access to the hay mazes, live entertainment, seasonal displays, photo opportunities and more, while attraction credits can be purchased at kiosks throughout the event.

About Boo Bash

Boo Bash is a seasonal pumpkin patch and family fall festival bringing together fall traditions, interactive attractions, games, entertainment, food and shopping in one destination.
